passage: Note to myself, Sunday night, after Sunaina Masi's visit. Masi had knitted Yamini a mustard-yellow sweater with a crooked green duck on the front. Yamini, who is nine and only wears blue, held it up for a long second. Then she hugged Masi and said, "I love it, it's so soft." Masi's whole face lit up. Later, in her room, Yamini asked me quietly, "Amma, was that a lie? I don't love it. But her face was so happy." I told her she had been kind, and that next time she could also find something true to say, like thanking Masi for all the hours of knitting. She wore it to the gate when Masi left.

qa.q: What was knitted on the front of the sweater?
qa.a: A crooked green duck was knitted on the front of the mustard-yellow sweater.

qa.q: Why did Yamini say she loved the sweater?
qa.a: Yamini cared about Masi and did not want to spoil her happiness; saying "her face was so happy" shows she was protecting Masi's feelings.

qa.q: What could Yamini try the next time she gets a gift she doesn't like?
qa.a: She could say something warm and true, such as thanking Masi for the hours of knitting, instead of claiming to love it.

qa.q: How might Sunaina Masi feel if she learned Yamini only wears blue?
qa.a: She might feel a little disappointed, but she would probably still value that Yamini hugged her and wore the sweater to the gate.

grounding: A child tells her aunt she loves a gift she dislikes, out of care, and starts to feel that kindness and truth can pull in different directions.

passage:
Dear Diary, Thursday.
Nazia aunty from next door brought a steel box of her new vegetable stew today. She watched me take the first spoon. It tasted like warm water with carrots in it. I said, "Mmm, aunty, super tasty!" She pinched my cheek and said, "Good girl, I'll make it again on Sunday, just for you."
JUST FOR ME. Now there will be more boxes.
I didn't want her to feel bad. She lives alone, and she was so excited, standing at our door in her apron. Mummy says being kind is good but I shouldn't say things I don't mean. I think next time I will say, "Thank you for thinking of me, aunty," because that part is true.
Indu

qa.q: What did Nazia aunty bring from next door?
qa.a: She brought a steel box of her new vegetable stew.

qa.q: What was Indu worried about after calling the stew super tasty?
qa.a: Indu worried that more boxes of the bland stew would come, because aunty promised to make it again on Sunday just for her.

qa.q: Which true sentence does Indu plan to use next time, and why might it work?
qa.a: Indu plans to say "Thank you for thinking of me, aunty", which is honest and still warm, so she can be kind without praising food she didn't enjoy.

qa.q: What is it like for Nazia aunty when Indu praises the stew?
qa.a: She feels happy and appreciated, especially since she lives alone, so she wants to cook it again for Indu.

grounding: A girl praises a neighbour aunty's bland dish to avoid hurting her, and notices the pull between being kind and being truthful.
